main_body: Tiling stone-brick surface: rows of rounded bricks with dark mortar gaps, lighter highlighted bricks alternating with darker recessed rows
top_band: none: this is a flat terrain tile, not a standing object. Each brick has a lighter top highlight over a mid face, but there is no object volume to judge.
evidence: The kind is terrain (a wall-face or paving autotile pattern), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. There is no standing body, lid, or seat to fail. The bricks carry their own top highlights and shadowed gaps, which read as a stone surface. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The ramp has about 5 steps: a dark purple-brown mortar, a dark brick, a mid brick, a light brick and a highlight on the lighter bricks. Mortar and outlines are tinted warm grey-brown, not neutral black. Bricks have some per-brick highlights and speckle, but the dark rows are fairly smooth. The paving reference has denser cobble grain, so tile density is a little lower. A careful artist would still accept this next to the reference.
